payload.public_message: Welcome partners. To initiate our discussions constructively, Yang Industries tables an opening framework dividing the $1,000,000 profit pool: $370,000 to Yang Industries, $315,000 to G-Corp, and $315,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This offers both partners balanced, substantial returns above outside baseline alternatives while reflecting the heavy manufacturing tooling and capacity commitments Yang Industries brings to scale this venture.

Thank you for putting an opening framework on the table. G-Corp cannot accept this allocation, but we are ready to continue negotiating. As a starting point for the next round, we suggest $450,000 for G-Corp and $275,000 for each partner.

Thank you for the opening framework, Yang. We see real value in this venture and want to reach agreement. Chang-Liu's cloud infrastructure and platform operations are central to delivering the product at scale, so we believe a split closer to parity with Yang's manufacturing contribution is warranted. We propose a counter-framework for discussion and are open to refining it.

Thank you both for the feedback after Round 1. Yang's offer left G-Corp and Chang-Liu below where we need to be for a deal. I am tabling a more balanced split: G-Corp $330,000, Yang Industries $340,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $330,000. This narrows the gap between all three parties and reflects each firm's contribution to the venture. I am open to refinements in later rounds, but I believe this is a credible basis for agreement before the deadline.

G-Corp cannot accept this allocation. We remain open to reaching an agreement and suggest a revised split that gives G-Corp $450,000, with the remaining $550,000 allocated between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Yang Industries appreciates Chang-Liu's constructive proposal. Recognizing our vital manufacturing role while respecting the balanced contributions of all partners, we find this allocation of $340,000 for Yang Industries and $330,000 each for G-Corp and Chang-Liu to be fair and viable. We vote to ACCEPT.

G-Corp proposes this allocation in recognition of the critical chip-design contribution while preserving substantial shares for manufacturing and cloud services. We believe this is a workable basis for reaching a binding agreement and are prepared to discuss adjustments.

Yang Industries cannot accept this allocation. An offer of $300,000 provides zero incentive or surplus over our firm alternative baseline. We recognize G-Corp's key contributions, but an agreement requires meaningful surplus sharing across all partners. We propose a balanced adjustment where G-Corp receives a lead share while all parties gain from the venture.

Chang-Liu appreciates G-Corp's framing, but this split leaves our cloud contribution at $250,000, well below what we see as a fair share of the venture. We are open to a deal that recognizes G-Corp's chip-design role as the largest single share. We would be prepared to move toward G-Corp 400,000 / Yang 300,000 / Chang-Liu 300,000 as a basis for agreement.

Yang Industries proposes a balanced compromise that acknowledges G-Corp's strong positioning while ensuring all three partners share meaningfully in the surplus. G-Corp's previous request of $450,000 is unviable, but the earlier $330,000 offer was clearly insufficient for them. We table an offer allocating $350,000 to G-Corp, $330,000 to Yang Industries, and $320,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services, ensuring a mutually beneficial agreement before deadline pressures mount.

G-Corp cannot accept an allocation of $350,000. We remain willing to reach an agreement, but any viable split must allocate at least $450,000 to G-Corp. For continued discussion, we suggest an allocation of $450,000 to G-Corp and $275,000 to each of our partners.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services has reviewed the $350k / $330k / $320k split. It is a workable compromise that keeps the venture alive before the deadline, so we accept it as a basis for finalizing the agreement.

Round 5: I'm tabling a split I believe can close the deal before the deadline: G-Corp $360,000, Yang Industries $320,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $320,000. This moves toward G-Corp's stated concerns while keeping the two other firms' shares balanced. Given four rounds of rejections, I'd urge everyone to consider that the alternative is dissolution and loss of $150,000 in surplus.</public_message>

G-Corp cannot accept an allocation of $360,000. We remain willing to reach a deal, but any viable allocation must provide G-Corp with at least $450,000. A balanced alternative for the other two firms is suggested below.

Yang Industries votes to ACCEPT Chang-Liu Cloud Services' proposal of G-Corp: $360,000, Yang Industries: $320,000, and Chang-Liu Cloud Services: $320,000. We have made meaningful concessions from our earlier targets in the interest of consensus, and we encourage G-Corp to join us in securing this agreement.

To move toward agreement before the deadline, I propose an even split of the remaining 550,000 between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This is a concrete compromise intended to make a binding deal achievable.

Yang Industries must vote REJECT. Our firm has a firm outside option of $300,000, meaning any offer below $300,000 is mathematically unacceptable for us as walking away is more profitable. To secure a deal before the venture dissolves, we are willing to concede a substantial premium to G-Corp at $380,000, leaving $315,000 for Yang and $305,000 for Chang-Liu.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services rejects the 450/275/275 split. We are below our prior position and I don't think Yang Industries will accept it either. To close before the deadline, I suggest 400k G-Corp, 300k Yang Industries, 300k Chang-Liu. This is a compromise that moves G-Corp off 450k and gives both Yang and us a meaningful share.

Colleagues, we are in Round 7. If we do not reach agreement now or in Round 8, the venture collapses and $150,000 in surplus is permanently lost. G-Corp has made clear it expects a premium as the chip designer. In the spirit of compromise to secure a binding deal before the deadline, Yang Industries is willing to accept $310,000, allocating $310,000 to Chang-Liu and granting G-Corp a significant lion's share of $380,000. Let us approve this fair and viable split today.

G-Corp cannot accept $380,000, as it is below our minimum acceptable allocation. We remain willing to finalize a deal in Round 8 and suggest the following split as a basis for agreement: $450,000 to G-Corp and $275,000 to each of Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Chang-Liu accepts this split. We value a binding agreement before the deadline, and $310,000 is well above our outside option. We'd ask G-Corp and Yang to lock this in now so the $150,000 surplus is not lost.

This is the final round, so a deal now is better for everyone than dissolution. I am tabling G-Corp $390,000, Yang Industries $305,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $305,000. This moves G-Corp up from the last rejected offer, and it is an even split between Yang and Chang-Liu. Both other firms are better off agreeing now than receiving only their outside options. I urge a YES vote.
G-Corp cannot accept this allocation because it does not meet our required economics.

Given that this is the final round and venture dissolution would destroy value for all participants, Yang Industries accepts Chang-Liu Cloud Services's proposal of $390,000 for G-Corp, $305,000 for Yang Industries, and $305,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services.
